stepExplanation: During depolarisation: (1) A stimulus causes the membrane to reach threshold (approximately -55mV), (2) Voltage-gated sodium (Na+) channels open rapidly, (3) Sodium ions rush INTO the cell down their concentration gradient (facilitated diffusion), (4) The inside of the membrane becomes positive (up to +40mV), (5) This is called DEPOLARISATION. The influx of positive sodium ions reverses the polarity of the membrane.
